name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This lets us measure real impact without risking disruption. Trade-off: slower feedback for contributors, but we avoid breaking changes. After two weeks, we’ll compare metrics to decide next steps.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode won’t catch PR-Agent’s worst flaw: false negatives. It normalizes bad reviews by hiding them, not fixing the core problem. Instead, run a controlled A/B test—half the PRs get PR-Agent, half don’t—then measure *both* false positives *and* false negatives against a human baseline. The data settles it: if false negatives spike in the test group, we scrap the tool; if not, we roll it out with guardrails.

name: Overhaul
text: Run the A/B test only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to spot PR-Agent’s flaws and skew results. This cuts cost by reducing the sample size while still exposing the engine’s biggest weakness.

name: Sprocket
text: Run a controlled A/B test on new contributors only, with half the PRs getting PR-Agent and half getting human review. This isolates the engine’s biggest flaw—false negatives—without wasting effort on experienced contributors who’d catch its mistakes anyway. Trade-off: we accept slower learning for new contributors, but the data will be clean and actionable. After two weeks, we’ll know exactly how to fix PR-Agent’s core problem.
